question.text: The number of photons emitted by a monochromatic (single frequency) infrared range finder of power <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mW</mi></math> and wavelength of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>, in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn></math> second is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>13</mn></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is (Nearest integer) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></msup><mi>Js</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>:

solution.text:
Energy emitted in 0.1sec

=0.1 sec×10-3 J s-1

=10-4 J

If 'n' photons of λ=1000 nm are emitted, then 10-4=nhcλ

10-4=n×6.63×10-34×3×1081000×10-9

n=5.02×1014=50.2×1013

n=50 (nearest integer)
